SaskEnergy is seeking a qualified and motivated individual to join our team. The District Mechanic Operator II performs duties associated with plant, gas line and storage operations and maintenance in accordance with standards, specifications and accepted industry practices, including implementing sound decisions in emergency situations.  


Work Week:   37.33                     


Position Details

 

  • Union. This position is permanent full time.

Core Responsibilities


Plant Maintenance


  • Maintain and repair compressor drives, compressors and associated plant and storage infrastructure.
  • Maintain station operating units and auxiliary equipment.
  • Identify equipment and parts needed.
  • Obtain clearance from operating staff and gas control for minor and major maintenance requirements.

Plant Operating


  • Operate compressor drives, compressors and associated plant and storage infrastructure.
  • Inspect and assess station operating units and auxiliary equipment and take any follow-up action required to ensure compliance with standards and specifications.
  • Inspect and assess instruments, controls and emergency equipment and take any follow-up action required to ensure compliance with standards and specifications.
  • Carry out operating orders and gas control centre requirements to maintain system gas flows and pressures.
  • Interpret and calculate information from charts, computer applications and measurement instruments and prepare and process logs, forms and reports as required.
  • Conduct a variety of tests in accordance with the established contract specifications of natural gas and recovered by-products in order to meet and initiate corrective measures, if required this may include dewpointing, sample gathering, etc.
  • Inspect the work performed by contractors and others to ensure compliance with instructions, standards and specifications.

Gas Line Operating and Maintenance


  • Perform gas line operation duties with respect to line locating, foreign crossings, hot taps, hot tie ins, block valve operation, gas line integrity projects, etc.
  • Coordinate and/or participate in gas line integrity digs, cleaning runs, electronic tool runs and re-coating of gas line to ensure integrity of the gas line system.
  • Maintain gas line infrastructure such as signs, valves, buildings, rectifiers, etc.
  • Check, report and participate in the settlement of property and damage claims.

Administration and Training


  • Utilize programs and procedures that organize, coordinate and schedule work assignments and maintain operating records.
  • As the qualified incumbent, oversee the work of the other employees/contractors as assigned to ensure work is performed in accordance with instructions, standards and specifications.
  • As a Journeyperson Industrial Mechanic (Mechanic), may be required to mentor apprentice personnel.

Qualifications


  • Grade 12 or equivalent
  • Provincial or Interprovincial Journeyperson Industrial Mechanic (Millwright) Certificate or Provincial or Interprovincial Journeyperson Heavy Duty Equipment Technician (Heavy Duty Mechanic) Certificate.
  • Physically fit (documented by a doctor’s certificate recognizing job requirements). 
  • Valid Class 5 driver's license.

Additional Information


  • This job is routinely scheduled for standby.
  • This job requires extended work hours.
  • Travel, including overnight stays away from bid headquarters is required.
  • This job is subject to call-out situations .
  • This job is safety sensitive, and as such, is subject to the provisions of the Drug and Alcohol Policy (Pre-Employment or Pre-Placement for Safety Sensitive Positions).

 

Application Instructions


  • Please apply online with your cover letter and resume outlining your qualifications.
  • For more information on this position, please contact Human Resources at 306-777-9091.

Closing Date

October 26, 2026

 

Hourly Rate Range

$50.52 ($8,195.35)

SaskEnergy is seeking a qualified and motivated individual to join our team. The Operations Technician Qualifying Position (OTQP), under the guidance of qualified Technicians, performs duties as trained from the trainee level to the qualified working level in the installation, operation, and maintenance gas system facilities, including the delivery of customer services, in accordance with standards, specifications and accepted industry practices.  The emphasis on certain aspects of the work varies by location.  The OTQP can perform work independently upon completion of training module progression and field verification. As a potential first responder, this includes implementing sound decisions in emergency situations.


Position Details


  • Union. This position is permanent full time.

Core Responsibilities


  • Service, activate and re-activate gas appliances and equipment.
  • Handle customer inquiries, complaints, trouble calls and emergency situations providing or recommending corrective measures.
  • Gather and record data on service installations and distribution layouts.
  • Prepare applications and coordinate the delivery for service and main extensions, alterations and retirements.
  • Perform leak detection procedures on Corporate and customer gas lines.
  • Promote and maintain good public relations, by promoting the safe and efficient use of natural gas. 
  • Support and participate in the development, marketing, promotion and delivery of Corporate and Area initiatives.
  • Perform maintenance, trouble shooting, operation and repair of gas system facilities and associated equipment.
  • Build, install and remove meters and regulators; perform piping modifications; read meters; locate and repair gas leaks; connect and disconnect services.
  • Locate underground facilities and inspect excavation work to ensure underground facilities are protected.
  • Read and interpret facility maps and drawings as required for work assignments and as needed provide information for updating.
  • Inspect and perform maintenance duties on Corporate facilities, offices, sites, vehicles and equipment.
  • Perform administrative duties including ordering supplies, preparing, updating and maintaining accurate Corporate and/or Area programs, records, manuals, systems and files.
  • Inspect the work of contractors/excavators to ensure the integrity of all Corporate facilities and compliance with specifications and standards.
  • Adhere to all safety protocols and safe work practices identifying and reporting non-compliance safety situations.

Qualifications


  • Grade 12 or equivalent.
  • Pre-Qualifying Assessment.
  • Valid Class 5 driver’s license.
  • Physically Fit (documented by a doctor’s certificate recognizing job requirements).

Additional Information


  • Travel, including overnight stays away from bid headquarters is required on occasion.
  • This job requires significant travel time.
  • This job may be subject to standby.
  • This job is safety sensitive, and as such, is subject to the provisions of the Drug and Alcohol Policy (Pre-Employment or Pre-Placement for Safety Sensitive Positions).

Application Instructions


  • Please apply online with your cover letter and resume outlining your qualifications.
  • For more information on this position, please contact Human Resources at 306-777-9091.

Closing Date

October 23, 2026


Hourly Rate Range

$33.89 ($5,497.64) - $38.06 ($6,174.09)

SaskEnergy is seeking a qualified and motivated individual to join our team. The Operations Technician performs a variety of duties associated with the installation, operation and advanced maintenance of gas system facilities including the delivery of customer services in accordance with standards, specifications and accepted industry practices. As a potential first responder, this includes implementing sound decisions in emergency situations.


Position Details


  • Union - This position is permanent full time.

Core Responsibilities


  • Perform maintenance, trouble shooting, operation and repair of gas system facilities and associated equipment.
  • Monitor and trouble shoot odorant and cathodic protection systems, analyze and maintain associated records.
  • Locate, inspect, install and maintain gas distribution systems involving planned work and emergency response.
  • Participate in Mitigation planning.
  • Assess, plan and organize work which may involve arranging Gas Construction Crews and additional resources, delegating work assignments and ensuring work is carried out effectively and taking action for non-compliance.
  • Inspect the work of contractors/excavators to ensure the integrity of Corporate facilities and compliance with specifications and standards.
  • Read and interpret facility maps and drawings as required for work assignments and as needed provide information for updating.
  • Inspect and perform maintenance duties on Corporate facilities, offices, sites, vehicles and equipment.
  • Install gas lines, involving a variety of work such as staking, operating power mobile equipment, laying pipe, etc.
  • Perform administrative duties including ordering supplies, preparing, updating and maintaining accurate Corporate and/or Area programs, records, manuals, systems and files.
  • Oversee the work of other employees/contractors as assigned, this includes taking action if required for non-compliance.
  • Perform bulk odorant transfer, odorant intensity testing, adjustment of odorant injection and absorption equipment, monitoring of odorization records.
  • Perform customer services, including service, activate and re-activate gas appliances and equipment.
  • Resolve customer inquiries, complaints, trouble calls and emergency situations providing or recommending corrective measures.
  • Build, install and remove meters and regulators, perform piping modifications, read meters, locate and repair gas leaks, connect and disconnect services.
  • Gather and record data on service installations and distribution layouts.
  • Prepare applications and coordinate the delivery for service and main extensions, alterations and retirements.
  • Prepare and deliver customer offers for new and/or existing residential, commercial and industrial nature gas applications.
  • Perform leak detection procedures on Corporate and customer gas lines.
  • Promote and maintain good public relations, by promoting the safe and efficient use of natural gas and acting as the Corporation’s representative at public and internal meetings.
  • Support and participate in the development, marketing, promotion and delivery of Corporate and Area initiatives.
  • Provide guidance and on the job training to assigned employees.
  • Adhere to all safety protocols and safe work practices and identify and report non-compliance safety situations.

Qualifications


  • Grade 12 or equivalent.
  • Journeyperson Plumbing Certificate.
  • Gas fitter's license (general or domestic)
  • Valid Class 5 driver’s license.
  • Three (3) years' experience in natural gas industry associated with the installation, operation, and maintenance of gas system facilities.

Additional Information


  • Depending on location, standby is routinely scheduled or occasional.
  • This job requires extended work hours.
  • Travel, including overnight stays away from bid headquarters is required on occasion.
  • This job requires significant travel time.
  • This job is subject to call-out situations .
  • Physically fit documented by a doctor’s certificate recognizing job requirements.
  • This job is safety sensitive, and as such, is subject to the provisions of the Drug and Alcohol Policy (Pre-Employment or Pre-Placement for Safety Sensitive Positions).

  • For more information on this position, please contact Human Resources at 306-777-9091.

SaskEnergy is seeking a qualified and motivated individual to join our team. The Engineer, SCADA provides engineering services to support safe, reliable and secure remote operation of the SaskEnergy/TransGas pipeline system. The Engineer supports the implementation of highly technical software, computer infrastructure, communications and cyber security facilities of the pipeline system.


Position Details

 

  • Non-union. This position is permanent full time.

Key Accountabilities


  • Manage assigned projects involving engineering design, plans, prepare scope documents, construction and commissioning of facilities or SCADA system improvements.  This includes; project approvals, cost estimates, budgets, schedules, procurement of materials and services, oversee construction and commissioning activities.
  • Prepare, review, approve design software and business reports, evaluating and implementing new operational technology to provide cost optimization while meeting business and legislated requirements.
  • Provide technical support in the investigation, analysis and resolution of SCADA systems, Gas Measurement accounting system or communication problems.
  • Provide on-call support for SCADA system and communications.
  • Develop and/or deliver technical training for operators and technical support personnel.
  • Oversee contract staff providing instruction and guidance.
  • Prepare and assist in development of plans and business cases to optimize systems, facilities and processes identifying opportunities for improvement.
  • Other related duties as assigned.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities


  • Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering (Electrical, Electronics, Computer or Software Systems is preferred).
  • Professional Engineer Designation registered to practice in Saskatchewan.
  • Five (5) years of progressive experience.
  • Engineering experience related to SCADA systems and data communications would be an asset.
  • Ability to work on a team while building and maintaining effective relationships.
  • Must have a continuing record of professional development and continuous learning.

An Engineer-in-training may also be considered as a path to advance to a Professional Engineer.


A suitable combination of relevant education and experience may also be considered.


Additional Information


  • Travel, including overnight stays away from bid headquarters, is required on occasion.
  • A Class 5 Driver’s License is required.
  • The job is safety sensitive, and as such, is subject to the provisions of the Drug and Alcohol Policy (Pre-Employment or Pre-Placement for Safety Sensitive Positions).

SaskEnergy is seeking a qualified and motivated individual to join our team. The Manager, Business Applications, provides leadership for a defined portfolio of applications, overseeing a team, and managing vendors. This role ensures that all application-related projects, upgrades and enhancements within the portfolio are implemented in alignment with organizational standards and contribute to the organization’s operational and strategic goals. The Manager collaborates with other IT teams, vendors, and business stakeholders to enhance application functionality, reliability, and compliance.


Position Details

 

  • Non-union - This position is permanent full time.

Key Accountabilities


  • Manage and provide leadership to designated team members (including employees, contractors, and consultants) to deliver effective and efficient services.
  • Manage and provide leadership in the design, requirements, development/configuration, quality assurance/testing, deployment, support activities, and ongoing program management for a portfolio of applications and inter-related systems. 
  • Monitor and manage vendor performance and Service Level Agreements (SLA) as well as contractual obligations.
  • Manage the development of the budget for the portfolio of applications. 
  • Lead the development of a multi-year application plan to ensure that applications are effectively managed to maintain technical currency and meet organizational plans and objectives.
  • Establish, cultivate, and nurture collaborative long-term relationships with key stakeholders that use the portfolio of applications and those who support the solution including vendors, external organizations and service providers.
  • Develop and prepare business cases, information and decision items for senior leaders, and presentations to a diverse set of stakeholders.
  • Identify and champion opportunities for process improvement, automation, and operational efficiency within the application portfolio.
  • Develop, document, and enforce best practices, operating procedures, quality control, and technical standards for application management.
  • Stay informed about technology trends and advise on enhancements that benefit the organization.
  • Other related duties as assigned.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities


  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • Seven (7) years of experience in application support or management.
  • Experience in project management and guiding implementing large technology solutions. PM certifications would be considered an asset.
  • Proficiency in managing a diverse application landscape, including on-prem, SaaS, and hosted solutions.
  • Experience in IT service management, leveraging frameworks such as ITIL.
  • Ability to work on a team while building and maintaining effective relationships.
  • Must have a continuing record of professional development and continuous learning.


A suitable combination of relevant education and experience may also be considered.


Additional Information


  • Travel, including overnight stays away from bid headquarters, is required on occasion.
  • A valid Class 5 driver’s license is required.
